executable_analysis.method: Parsed PE32+ .pdata runtime-function table and disassembled code ranges from the supplied executable; read-only.
measured_dataflow: Function 00637660 saves its incoming R9 in RBX and supplies that same value as R9 when calling 00637DB0 at 006377A3.
Function 00637DB0 saves incoming R9 in R14, then passes R14 as the first stack argument to 006377E0 at 00637F1F.
At entry to 006377E0, that value is read from its first stack argument into RDX and passed as the source pointer to 00227A40 at 00637892; destination is object+0x128.
Function 00227A40 reads source descriptor fields at offsets +0x4, +0x8, +0x10 and +0x20 while initializing/copying into the destination object.
Thus the descriptor copied into object+0x128 comes from the R9 input to 00637660 along the observed static call chain.
The direct caller at 02D042E1 sets R9 to local address [rbp-0x28]; the direct caller at 02D04AF8 sets R9 to [rbp-0x38]; the caller at 001B2CF9 sets R9 to [rbp-0x20].

At 02D042E1 the local source record is populated from a preceding 32-byte copy and zero-initialized fields; at 02D04AF8 a local 32-byte record is assembled from a calculated 16-byte value and zeroed fields. The visible code does not identify these records as the live derelict root descriptor.
executable_analysis.interpretation: The static data flow now identifies the wrapper's descriptor-source parameter precisely: it is the incoming R9 pointer, forwarded through 00637DB0 to 006377E0 and copied by 00227A40. This is a more specific conclusion than the earlier generic 'upstream descriptor argument' description. The three callers prepare distinct local records. No evidence yet ties any of those three caller paths to the live NMS root-resource event, current root seed 5B4AE67D9C2A8F61, or the universe address. The candidate remains unverified as a derivation.

That local qword was computed from the sign-extended 32-bit value at global-manager pointer 0x145029FC0+0x74 through xor-right-33 / multiply-by-0x64DD81482CBD31D7 / xor-right-33 / multiply-by-0xE36AA5C613612997 / xor-right-33. The +0x18 byte is initialized to 1.
caller_001B2CF9.derived_check: Inverting this exact mixer for root candidates 5B4AE67D9C2A8F61, 9256392A2F5A74AC, and 00C9E8DF0327789E yields inverse inputs 378CE29B6CD8B212, 6ECEE5395C48AD87, and F86D1AC5581C5D11. None is a sign-extended 32-bit integer.
caller_001B2CF9.interpretation: Assuming the static copy flow is unchanged, this specific caller/mixer path cannot directly emit those root candidates from its 32-bit input. It is excluded as a direct source for those candidate values; this does not exclude the other wrapper callers or a later transform.

measured_static_facts: Caller site 02D042E1 is inside .pdata range 02D0400B..02D0455C and calls wrapper 00637660 with R9 pointing to local record [rbp-0x28].
Caller site 02D04AF8 is inside .pdata range 02D04690..02D04F47 and calls wrapper 00637660 with R9 pointing to local record [rbp-0x38].
Both caller paths assemble a seed-like 64-bit value and call shared helper 02D03EE0. This helper is in .pdata range 02D03EE0..02D0400B.

The caller of helper 02D03EE0 at 02D03D41 belongs to .pdata range 02D03CCA..02D03ECC; it passes a context pointer loaded from [rbp+0x148] in R9 and an integer loaded from [rbp+0x150] as a stack argument.
The enclosing function for 02D04AF8 is called from function range 02D053A0..02D05DC0 at 02D0552D; that enclosing function calls helper 02D03EE0 again at 02D05ACE.

interpretation.inference: The remaining wrapper callers share a context-based seed-building/helper path and appear to serve generated-resource processing.
interpretation.unknown: Static data does not reveal dynamic values behind the context pointers or establish whether either call creates the live derelict root resource.
interpretation.conclusion: Neither path proves a universe-address-to-root-seed derivation. A runtime observation of descriptor input during the root event may be needed if further static dispatch analysis does not establish object identity.
